title: Grading Improvements | Clo 2026.0 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new update in CLO 2026.0 allows you to select and edit multiple fields simultaneously within the Grading Table, and apply irregular deviation values all at once using formulas. 
Check out other new features here:https://clo3d.com/en/clo/features

markdown_content: ## Grading UI: Turn On and Display Grading Tools This section explains how to enable grading in **CLO** and where to find the **grading tab**, including the **toggle menu** option to show grading even when you are not in the grading tools workspace. - In **CLO**, open the **grading** area and ensure **grading** is turned on. - Go to the **Grading** tab so the **grading tools** become active. - Even if you are not currently in the grading tools or grading tab, you can still view grading via the **toggle menu**. - In the garment view area (under the **T-shirt garment display**), use the **Show Grading** option to display grading-related controls and measurements. ## The Grading Window: Posting Test Releases and Editing Rules This section covers the **grading window** used to post a **test release**, how to pop it out, and how grading rules can be arranged either in the window or in the **property editor**. - The **grading window** is used to **post a test release**. - You can **pop the grading window out** for a dedicated editing space. - **Exit** moves the grading rules to the **side** in the **property editor**. - Both layouts are supported: - Rules aligned in the popped-out grading window. - Rules listed in the **property editor** when the window is exited. ## Measurement Controls: Aspect Ratio, Arrow Keys, and Units This section describes key controls for editing measurements, including aspect ratio locking, arrow-key movement increments, and unit context (inches vs. other units). - You can **lock aspect ratio** (and **unlock** it when needed). - Arrow-key movement is configurable: - Each arrow-key press moves by a set increment. - The increment shown in the session is **0.25**. - Units depend on your setup: - The session indicates **inches** are being used (US context). ## Editing Multiple Measurements with Shift + Double-Click This section explains how to edit multiple measurements at once using **Shift + double-click**, and how that differs from editing a single measurement without Shift. ### Select multiple measurements and apply a single value - Hold **Shift** to select multiple measurements simultaneously. - **Double-click** the selected measurement group. - Enter a new value and press **Enter**. - Example behavior shown: - When three measurements were set together to **2.15**, they updated to **2.15** in the top group. ### Difference vs. editing without Shift - If you **do not** hold **Shift** and instead set a value directly (e.g., **2.15**), then the measurement directly below may also change. - Holding **Shift** before double-clicking allows more controlled updates: - Only the intended selected measurements update. - Some adjacent measurements may remain unchanged depending on selection and context. ## Negative Values and Correcting Irregular Grading This section covers how negative measurement entries behave and how to fix or interpret “irregular grading” cases using Shift-based selection. - The workflow supports entering negative values (e.g., **-2.15**). - If results look incorrect, re-check the selection method: - Use **Shift + double-click** to ensure only the intended measurements are targeted. - Example shown: irregular grading where one size changes but another does not. - Hold **Shift**, select the relevant measurement, then double-click. - Release **Shift**, enter the new value (e.g., **4**), and press **Enter**. - Only the intended size/measurement changes; the other does not. ## Red Highlighting: Detecting Measurement Mismatches This section explains why measurements can turn **red**, indicating a mismatch between expected relationships (e.g., sizes that should match but do not). - **Red highlighting** indicates an issue: the measurements do not match expected constraints. - Example described: - Two measurements were expected to be the same (e.g., sizes that should match), - but after changing one size, the pair no longer matched. - The red state is essentially a warning that the current grading values are inconsistent with the rule/expectation that those measurements should align. ## Applying Values to Multiple Measurements (Example: 9.5) This section provides an example of using Shift-based multi-selection to apply a single value to multiple measurements without affecting others. - To update only specific measurements: - Hold **Shift** and select the target measurements. - Hold **Shift** and double-click the selected group. - Enter a value (example: **9.5**) and press **Enter**. - The example behavior indicates only the selected measurements change, while others remain unaffected.
